title: Pocket allocator with deferred scavenger for low-fragmentation KV cache
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: As long-running inference workloads and continuous batching patterns evolve, the KV cache on GPUs exhibits long-tail internal fragmentation. This increases peak GPU memory usage and forces early evictions that degrade P95 latency for chat workloads. Existing slab and region allocators reduce churn but still leave small, unusable holes under mixed token lengths and multi-tenant traffic.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight per-stream 'pocket' allocator combined with a deferred scavenger (deferred scan + bounded live migration) that runs during low-util windows. Key ideas: pockets are small pre-allocated buckets attached to worker threads / SM groups to service frequent small allocations without touching the global free lists, reducing cross-thread fragmentation and spin contention. The deferred scavenger walks GPU-side pocket metadata and performs generational migration of live KV fragments into contiguous target slabs when global occupancy crosses thresholds. The scavenger is rate-limited, cooperative with continuous-batching (batch-stickiness hints), and preserves kernel alignment to avoid extra copies during attention kernels.

Goals: reduce fragmentation overhead (free-but-unusable memory) by >=30% on typical chat workloads, keep P95 token latency regression <5% during background scans, and reduce eviction churn that causes context recomputation for long-lived sessions.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests show >=30% reduction in measured fragmentation metric (fragmented_bytes / total_allocated) on two benchmark workloads (multi-tenant chat and streaming completion).
P95 generation latency increase during background scavenger <= 5% compared to baseline under steady traffic.
KV hit-rate and prefix reuse metrics are unchanged or improved (no negative impact on cache effectiveness).
Telemetry dashboards created: pocket-utilization, scavenger-throughput, fragmentation-histogram, migration-latency.
Canary rollout plan produced and executed: 5% traffic for 24h, verify metrics, then 25% for 48h before global rollout.
tasks: Design: finalize pocket size heuristics and pocket-to-slab mapping (Ava/Liam) - design doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/KV/Pocket+Allocator+Design
Prototype: implement per-worker pocket allocator (GPU-side metadata + minimal host control) - PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
Telemetry: add fragmentation histogram and per-pocket occupancy counters to console metrics
Deferred scavenger: implement rate-limited GPU kernel that migrates hot fragments into target slabs and updates indirections
Continuous-batching integration: add batch-stickiness hint to allocator API so batched requests prefer contiguous allocations
Stress tests: run mixed token-length, multi-tenant scenarios on staging (2x, 5x load) and record metrics
Canary rollout: prepare experiment, safety checks, and rollback plan
Docs & runbook: update operator runbook with scavenger knobs and emergency disable flow
decisions: Use per-worker pockets (attached to inference threads) rather than per-GPU global tiny-bin caches to minimize cross-thread contention.
Perform live migration in-place where possible using indirection tables instead of wholesale copy-on-move to limit pause times.
Rate-limit deferred scavenger by time-slice and GPU-util heuristic (scavenger backs off if CUDA SM occupancy > threshold).
Expose two knobs: pocket_size_hint (bytes) and scavenger_aggressiveness (0..10) in runtime config for tuning.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces fragmentation and allocation contention, improved steady-state memory efficiency, lower eviction churn for long sessions.
Cons: additional GPU-side metadata and a background kernel introduce a small constant memory overhead (~1-2% of GPU memory) and implementation complexity.
Mitigation: metadata is compact (16 bytes per pocket) and scavenger is disabled by default for small instances; conservative defaults chosen for safety.
notes: Relation to prior work: this is complementary to slab rebalancing (ENG-31845) and slot anchoring (ENG-21731) — pockets reduce micro-fragmentation while rebalancers handle macro-level slab skew.

We will instrument continuous-batching path to emit allocation locality hints: allocations created during the same batch are marked 'sticky' so scavenger preserves their locality unless migration yields clear memory savings.
Prototype on an A100-like profile first; validate on RTX and H100 profiles for kernel alignment sensitivity.
Consider future extension: make pockets NUMA-aware for multi-GPU nodes and expose per-tenant pocket isolation for Dedicated deployments.

2026-03-08 - Design review (Samantha Ortiz): Approved overall approach; asked for clearer metrics in dashboard and that indirection updates are atomic to avoid serving stale KV entries. Liam to add fencing semantics in PR.
